reuse.why: Collapses the five provider link bodies into one linkBankSyncAccount and puts the new Fintegra link on it, but releaseAccountLinks re-writes the unlinkAccount field reset and downloadFintegraTransactions copies downloadAkahuTransactions instead of sharing it.

duplication.why: Upgrade/create/sync duplication is removed, but the closed-account check runs both in assertBankAccountNotLinked and inside linkBankSyncAccount, releaseAccountLinks duplicates unlinkAccount's update block, and the Fintegra downloader is an Akahu copy.

placement.why: Link rules and the shared link flow sit in accounts/app.ts and provider sync in sync.ts as the tree does; the closed-account rule is placed in a function named for the duplicate-link check.

scope.why: All edits serve the five requested steps (refactor, duplicate guard, Fintegra, closed guard, takeover flag) plus tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: One link flow is much easier to own; the redundant closed check, the overloaded assert helper (validates, then returns ids to release) and the copied unlink/download code are small liabilities.

bypasses_abstraction.where: releaseAccountLinks re-implements the account reset of unlinkAccount instead of sharing it

disguised_duplication.where: releaseAccountLinks is a renamed copy of unlinkAccount's db.updateAccount reset; the closed-account rule is repeated in assertBankAccountNotLinked and linkBankSyncAccount

abstraction_drift.where: linkBankSyncAccount gains accountIdsToRelease and a closed-account branch; assertBankAccountNotLinked gains replaceExistingLink and a closed-target check; all six providers call both helpers
